The flooding of Harrisburg can be traced as far back as the year 1785 when the town was officially founded by John Harris (son of the first settler). Numerous floods have been reported since that year. Prior to the 1972 Flood, the Flood of 1936 was the flood of record for Harrisburg. It is reported that the River crested at approximatedly 319 feet (mean sea level at the Nagle Street gauge station in South Harrisburg). In comparison, the 1972 Flood crested at 322 feet, 3 full feet above the previous record. The flow at its peak was estimated at 1,020,000 cubic feet per second at the Nagle Street gauge. It is estimated that this degree of flooding will occur only once in every 400 years.
